entries.title: Psalms 42:1
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
1 David's zeal to serve God in the temple. 5 He encourages his soul to trust in God.

A.M. 2983. B.C. 1021. (Title.){Maschil,} or a Psalm giving instruction, of the sons, etc. Or, "An instructive Psalm," or didactic ode, "for the sons of Korah." It is generally supposed to have been written by David when driven from Jerusalem and beyond Jordan, by Absalom's rebellion.

the sons. 44:1; 45:1; 46:1; 47:1; 48:1; 49:1; 84:1; 85:1; *titles Nu 16:1,32; 26:11; 1Ch 6:33-37; 25:1-5 panteth. Heb. brayeth. so panteth. 63:1,2; 84:2; 143:6,7; Isa 26:8,9

entries.title: Psalms 42:7
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
Deep calleth. Job 1:14-19; 10:17; Jer 4:20; Eze 7:26 water-spouts.A water-spout is a large tube formed of clouds by means of the electric fluid, the base being uppermost, and the point let down perpendicularly form the clouds. It has a particular kind of circular motion at the point; and, being hollow within, attracts vast quantities of water, which it frequently pours down in torrents upon the earth. These spouts are frequent on the coast of Syria; and no doubt the Psalmist had often seen them, and the ravages which they made.

all thy. 69:14,15; 88:7,15-17; La 3:53-55; Jon 2:3
